title: How Lizzie Borden Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Jerry back in the studio) cover the 1892 Fall River, Massachusetts murders of Andrew Borden and Abby Borden, and the trial of his daughter Lizzie Borden. They describe the Borden house layout, the family's financial tensions and bad mutton, the prussic acid purchase, the paint-stained dress, the missing hatchet handle, the trial evidence that was thrown out, the not-guilty verdict, and Lizzie's later life and death. The episode ends with a listener letter from Andrew in Utah about a skin infection and how people react to facial differences.

segments.title: Opening banter and episode setup
segments.summary: Josh, Chuck and Jerry trade banter about Jerry's return and the studio atmosphere, then introduce the Lizzie Borden case and tease the episode.

segments.title: The Borden house and family background
segments.summary: The hosts describe the August 4 morning in Fall River, Andrew Borden's return home, and his wealth and frugality. They describe the house's layout with locked doors and no indoor plumbing, plus the family history of Lizzie, Emma, and their mothers.

segments.title: Family tensions and the mutton illness
segments.summary: The family ate five-day-old mutton and was sick. Abby suspected poisoning. Andrew's stinginess and property dealings strained relations, and the pigeon killing and Uncle John Morse's visit added to the tension.

segments.title: The murders and the discovery of the bodies
segments.summary: Andrew Borden is killed on the sofa around 10:45 to 11 am; Abby is found upstairs after Bridget and a neighbor go up. Lizzie says she was in the barn loft eating pears. The bodies were autopsied and decapitated.

segments.title: Suspicion, the burned dress, and the hatchet evidence
segments.summary: Lizzie is the only person in the house during the likely time of Abby's murder. Alice Russell saw Lizzie burning a paint-stained dress. Police found hatchets in the basement, one missing its handle, with no blood found on the head.

segments.title: Blood evidence and possible explanations
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the problem of blood on the killer's clothing and the theory that Lizzie changed clothes between the murders.

segments.title: The trial and acquittal
segments.summary: At the trial, the prussic acid and Lizzie's testimony were excluded, forensic science was limited, and the case was largely circumstantial. The jury acquitted her after about 90 minutes. The skulls were displayed in court and Lizzie fainted.

segments.title: Alternative theories and Lizzie's later life
segments.summary: The hosts review theories about who killed the Bordens, including Lizzie in a fugue state, the maid, Emma, Uncle John, and an illegitimate son. They describe Lizzie's shunning in town, her move to Maplecroft, her estrangement from Emma, and the family deaths.

segments.title: Listener mail from Andrew in Utah
segments.summary: A listener describes a skin infection that affects his face and how people react to it, and thanks the hosts. The hosts wish listeners a happy new year.
